due_when.clears_when: scripts/ops/merge_json_register.py asserts PER ROW on `state`, `prs` and `blocked_on` — not only on note content — and a planted case where the two sides' notes merge cleanly while those three scalars disagree either resolves in the branch's favour for that lane's own row or REFUSES. A resolver that prints the scalar difference and proceeds does NOT clear this: printing is what already happened.

git log --all --grep='Merge origin/main' --format=%H -- docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json | head -20 | while read sha; do python3 - "$sha" <<'EOF'
# For each register merge: for every row, compare state/prs/blocked_on on the MERGE RESULT
# against BOTH parents. Report any row where the result matches neither parent's scalar or
# silently takes the non-branch side for a lane's OWN row.
EOF
done

what: A REGISTER MERGE CAN BE ENTIRELY RIGHT ABOUT THE PROSE AND SILENTLY WRONG ABOUT THE FIELDS NEXT TO IT, and the fields are the half that is read by machines. OBSERVED, not theorised: the manager merged origin/main into PR #12738 with a resolver that merges `note` per row and takes every other scalar from the longer-note side. E32's note CONCATENATED correctly — the lane verified by MARKER rather than length ('THE SIX LAYERS, IN DESCENDING AUTHORITY', 'LIST-observable fact', 'MAPPING LANDED' all present) — while three scalars beside it reverted: `state` blocked -> queued, `prs` [12738] -> [], and the blocked_on edge to E31 dropped. THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT COSMETIC: docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json is served to the operator as the live Workflow page via GET /api/bot/work/checklist. For as long as that stood, the page said 'scoped and agreed, nobody started it' with NO PR LINK about a row whose work was finished and sitting in an open PR. The prose is where a human looks and where the merge effort goes; `state`, `prs` and `blocked_on` are what the page and the guards READ. [!] IT IS NARROWER AND NASTIER THAN BL-20260814 and than the 'longer does not mean superset' lesson already recorded today. Both of those are about losing TEXT. This one loses nothing a reader would notice — the note grew — while inverting the row's machine-readable state. [!] THE FIX IS CHEAP AND THE LANE NAMED IT: for a lane's OWN row, the branch side is authoritative on exactly those three fields, so the assertion costs one comparison per row. scripts/ops/merge_json_register.py (E43's driver, landing as #12759) is where it belongs — it already resolves the header by kind, and this is the same idea one level down. [!] THE REPORTER CORRECTED ITSELF FIRST, which is why the diagnosis is trustworthy: its own first read saw E32's note jump 1,635 -> 7,174 chars and concluded 'main won wholesale, my update discarded'. Length is not provenance. Checking content flipped the conclusion. Anyone auditing other lanes' rows after these merges should check MARKERS, not sizes — a row can grow AND have lost something.
